title: Exploring the electrophysiology of Parkinson's disease - magnetoencephalography combined with deep brain recordings from the subthalamic nucleus.
description: This dataset comprises simultaneous magnetoencephalography (MEG) and subthalamic nucleus (STN) local field potential (LFP) recordings from externalized deep brain stimulation (DBS) patients with Parkinson's disease. Recordings were performed both with and without dopaminergic medication, across resting-state and movement conditions (forearm extension hold and self-paced fist-clenching). The study aims to elucidate the neurophysiology of basal ganglia-cortex loops and how they are modulated by movement and medication status.
methods_description: Data were collected via simultaneous MEG and STN LFP recordings from externalized DBS patients under two medication states (MedOn/MedOff). Recording sessions included resting-state periods and movement tasks: static forearm extension (hold) and self-paced fist-clenching (move), each preceded by 5 minutes of rest, with pauses during the movement segments. Some patients underwent resting-state recordings only.

funding_references.funder_name: The project was funded by ERA-NET Neuron for 3 years.
